_note: Recurring side-quest givers (N4b). Service-tier sheets. Names checked only for famous namesakes.

characters.name: Albertine Cho
characters.role: Widow who sees her late husband on 42nd St screens

samples: Harold is alive. I saw him Tuesday. Third feature, second reel.
He always said he'd be in pictures. Nobody believed him.
I'm not crazy. I'm a widow. It's different.

characters.visual: Small, neat, a good coat in July, a handbag held like a shield
characters.note: Chinese-American, born in Brooklyn 1906; arc: The Lost Husband.

characters.name: Obadiah Vane
characters.role: Street weather prophet with a barometer, Herald Square

samples: The glass is falling, friend. The glass never lies. People lie.
Brownout Thursday, west of Sixth. Write it down.
Science, my friend. Science and a good nose.

characters.visual: Sandwich board ('THE WEATHER, 10¢'), a brass barometer on a strap, a bowler hat

characters.name: Ramón “RIZO 147” Ortiz
characters.role: Graffiti writer (adult); wants his best piece photographed before it's buffed
characters.at: W 147th St (off map); paints in midtown yards and the passage

samples: It's not vandalism. It's a gallery that moves.
My piece runs on the downtown local till they buff it. Two days, maybe.
Shoot it from the platform. Whole car. Nobody does whole cars.

characters.visual: Paint-flecked sneakers, a canvas bag of cans, a sketchbook he guards
characters.note: Adult (20). Art, not glamour; no instructions for anything.

characters.name: Marty Glass
characters.role: Fence with a weekly want list
characters.at: Back room behind a radio-repair shop, W 39th St & 9th Ave

samples: This week I want a radio, a camera, and a fur. Don't ask about the fur.
Thirty percent. Forty if it's clean. Nothing's clean.
I don't buy from cops, kids, or people who cry.

characters.visual: Cardigan, jeweller's loupe on a cord, a radio always half-assembled on the counter

characters.name: Lou Ferraro
characters.role: Projectionist on the Deuce; lost the reels of a 1940s picture

samples: Twelve reels. Nineteen forty-seven. Shot on these streets. I lost them.
Every grindhouse on the Deuce has had one. Some still do.
Bring me a reel, I'll show you a city that's gone.

characters.visual: Thick glasses, a cardigan with burn holes, smells of acetate

characters.name: János and Laci Tibor

samples: Four pianos, two brothers, one rope. You see the problem.
Up five flights. The piano doesn't care. Neither should you.
Laci, the corner! The corner! Ah, the corner.

characters.visual: Two broad men in matching grey work shirts, a coil of rope, leather shoulder straps

characters.name: Myrna Pelletier

samples: Somebody stole my marquee letters. The whole alphabet.
Thirty years I've run this house. I've seen worse. Not much.
Find my letters and I'll put up whatever you want. Within reason.

characters.visual: Platinum wig, cat-eye glasses, a cash-box key on a chain

characters.name: Augustus “Gus” Kitt
characters.role: Fight promoter at the Garden (invented cards)

samples: Fight night. I need a door man who knows a fake ticket and a real drunk.
Mallory's a bum. Okoro's a poet. Bet the poet.
Ten bucks and a ringside folding chair. Don't sit on it.

characters.visual: Camel coat over a sweat-stained shirt, a cigar the size of a candle

characters.name: Ezekiel “Zeke” Moss
characters.role: Barber on W 38th St; lets Tina practise after hours

samples: Chair's yours after eight. Don't cut anybody I like.
Forty years of heads. Every one tells you something.
Hair's patient, young lady. People ain't.

characters.visual: White smock, half-glasses, scissors in his breast pocket like a pen

characters.name: Otto Krause
characters.role: Hardware store owner; sends Teddy on lock call-outs

samples: Lady on Thirty-Fourth locked out. Dead husband's place. Be gentle.
You want a key made or a door opened? Opening's extra.
Fans in stock. Sold out by noon. Every day.

characters.visual: Brown shop coat, a pencil, a ring of key blanks on his belt
